stem:
Ibuprofen and paracetamol are pain-relief drugs.

{{figure:pdf_visual_01.png}}

parts.label: (a)
parts.text:
Ibuprofen and paracetamol both contain the aryl (benzene) functional group.

Name the **other** functional groups present in each molecule.

parts.label: (b)
parts.stem: Ibuprofen contains a chiral centre and shows stereoisomerism.

parts.label: (b)(i)
parts.text: State what is meant by the term *chiral centre*.

parts.label: (b)(ii)
parts.text:
Draw the two stereoisomers of ibuprofen.

{{figure:pdf_visual_02.png}}

parts.label: (c)
parts.text:
Draw the structures of the organic products when ibuprofen and paracetamol react separately with $\text{LiAlH}_4$.

{{figure:pdf_visual_03.png}}

parts.label: (d)
parts.stem:
A student carried out some reactions with solutions of ibuprofen and paracetamol using reagents **D** and **E** and the following results were obtained. ($\checkmark$ means a reaction took place.)

| reagent | ibuprofen | paracetamol |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **D** | $\checkmark$ | $x$ |
| **E** | $x$ | $\checkmark$ |

parts.label: (d)(i)
parts.text: Suggest a possible identity for each reagent **D** and **E**.

parts.label: (d)(ii)
parts.text:
Give the structure of the organic product formed when reagent **D** reacted with ibuprofen.

{{figure:pdf_visual_04.png}}

parts.label: (d)(iii)
parts.text:
Give the structure of the organic product formed when reagent **E** reacted with paracetamol.

{{figure:pdf_visual_05.png}}

parts.label: (e)
parts.stem:
One of the steps in the manufacture of ibuprofen is shown.

{{figure:pdf_visual_06.png}}

parts.label: (e)(i)
parts.text: Write an equation for the reaction between $\text{CH}_3\text{COCl}$ and $\text{AlCl}_3$.

parts.label: (e)(ii)
parts.text:
Complete the mechanism for the conversion of **X** into **Y**. Include all necessary curly arrows, any relevant dipoles and charges.

{{figure:pdf_visual_07.png}}
